description: part2 v0: Part 1 champion spec refit natively on emerging (no changes)
part2 bar: developed base alone (Part 1 spec fit on developed 2021-23), level balanced on train, level-neutral metric, folds B+R

E1 region credibility factor — the base has never seen E01-E06 and diagnostics.md flags region E04 PERSISTENT on contents (A/E 1.17 B / 1.91 R, 4.2% exposure), and region is the top untried Tier 0 backlog item.

P0 — sum of the fine per-peril developed bases at level 1 (no emerging-fitted shrinkage) vs. the single total-cost base, since for buildings/contents (and motor's fine-split "other" perils) each `base_<peril>` is its own independent refit, not an algebraic share of `base`.

P1 — peril_levels(k=100) per line on top of kept P0, letting each peril's emerging/base cost ratio move (credibility-shrunk by claim count towards the line's overall ratio) instead of freezing every level at 1.0.

Re-test backlog E1 (region credibility factor) — the first attempt (2026-10-25T01:45:52, discard 0.13515) used raw y/base per region level, baking the developed-to-emerging level gap into the factor instead of isolating the relativity; `credibility_factors()` already normalises A/E to the line's own A/E before shrinking, so this retry applies it correctly, and the backlog explicitly says to re-test it first before moving on.

Backlog P2 — peril_levels(k=100) on motor only, since P1's loss (0.13820 < kept P0 0.13778) came from letting every peril move, including buildings fire which the backlog flags as noisy; motor glass/hail is the one clearly shifted peril (O6: 1.6-1.8x developed frequency).

Backlog P3 — peril_levels(k=30) on motor only, retrying the better of P1 (every line, 0.13820) / P2 (motor only, 0.13823) at less shrinkage, since both already nudged the primary above kept P0 (0.13778) but under the 0.001 keep margin.

backlog P4 — geometric blend (w=0.5) of `base` and the P2 motor-level peril-sum, since the two fold winners split (bar wins fold B, kept P0 wins fold R) and P1-P3's k sweep on motor peril levels is already near its shrinkage floor (z>0.9), so no more k values are worth testing.

E3 — joint ridge log-link Tweedie GLM correction (region, age band, new_business, channel, +cover_type on motor) on top of the kept P0 peril-sum base, alpha=10, since marginal credibility factors on region (E1) and age band (owner check) both lost on both folds, plausibly because region and new_business are confounded on a 76%-new-business broker book and a joint fit can net that out where univariate factors can't.

Backlog E4 — hail_days/wildfire_index sit far outside the developed training range (part2_drift.md PSI 1.8-6.5, motor glass_hail frequency 1.55-1.84x developed), so the base's trees extrapolate flat there; untried while E1/E3 discarded and E2 owner-ruled-out.

backlog E5 (renewal_count capped at 3) — untried; the owner's manual check only tested new_business by count (+0.0003, noise), and reports/part2_drift.md shows renewal_count/customer_tenure PSI from emg_train to the 2025 test rows is 2.0-2.1 on every line, the largest train/test shift in the drift table, since 76% of 2025 is new business.

backlog E6 — sum insured credibility factor on buildings/contents, since contents sum insured averages 113k vs 125k developed and 2025 buildings sum insured is 731k vs 680k in training (reports/part2_drift.md), a size-of-risk shift the base's banded relativity may not carry correctly; next untried Tier 0 item (E1/E3/E4/E5 all tried and discarded).

E7 — a tiny whitelisted LightGBM correction (region, age band, hail_days, wildfire_index, new_business) on top of kept P0, since every Tier 0 univariate credibility factor lost on both folds but can't net out confounding the way a joint model can.

E10 — per-line switch, peril-sum only on motor (where it helped fold B in kept P0) and plain `base` on buildings/contents (where the per-peril refits added estimation noise), since no per-line R split exists in the ledger to know which line carried P0's R gain.

E8 (backlog Tier 1) — an EBM correction on the same five-field whitelist that broke LightGBM (E7, discard 0.12431) should avoid that failure mode because it is additive with zero interactions and coarsely binned, so it can't carve out the noisy category combinations a multi-way tree split can.

backlog Tier 2 E11 — geometric blend of the kept P0 peril-sum base with `native` (iaa.experiment.fit_predict refit directly on emerging train data), since every Tier 0/1 structured correction (E1-E10) lost on both folds but a small dose of the native fit's ranking signal, heavily shrunk, hasn't been tried.

Stack the ledger's two best-performing corrections multiplicatively (backlog E12) — P3's motor peril_levels(k=30) and E5's renewal_count-capped-at-3 count-basis credibility factor — since both individually landed closest to beating kept P0 and act on orthogonal fields (motor glass/hail mix vs. tenure shift across all lines).

credibility factor on motor `fuel_type` (diesel 29.5% exposure, A/E 1.13 fold B / 1.11 fold R, PERSISTENT in diagnostics.md) on top of kept P0, since no Tier 0 factor tried so far targeted a large persistent diagnostic miss — E1/E5/E6 all hit fields the diagnostics table doesn't flag PERSISTENT.

Combine E3's joint GLM (region/age_band/new_business/channel/cover_type) with E4's weather signal as standardised numerics in the same model, since both individually came within ~0.001–0.0012 of beating kept P0 and backlog E4 explicitly suggests this fold-in, which hasn't been tried.

Stack the motor-only fuel_type credibility factor (03:21:06, discard 0.13877, short of the keep margin by 0.00001) onto the kept E12 pair (03:16:40, discard 0.13852: P3's motor peril_levels k=30 × E5's renewal_count-capped-at-3 factor), since the three act on orthogonal fields and the ledger shows the first two stacked additively.

Backlog P3's second named value, k=300 (more shrinkage) for motor peril_levels, is untried — only k=30 was tested (2026-10-25T02:39:25, discard 0.13830) and then carried into the kept champion stacked with E5's renewal factor and the fuel factor.

Stack a motor `cover_type` cost-basis credibility factor (k=200) onto the kept champion (E12 peril-levels+renewal+fuel, primary 0.13948), since diagnostics against that champion flags third_party_fire_theft (10.7% exposure) PERSISTENT with a wider both-fold A/E gap (0.857 B / 0.874 R) than the fuel_type miss that already passed, and cover_type has only three levels so little overfit risk, unlike region/occupation which lost.

motor-only elevation_m quintile credibility factor (cost basis, k=200, fuel_type's exact recipe) — diagnostics.md against the current champion flags elevation_m PERSISTENT at both tails (15.3-60: A/E 0.83 B/0.80 R, 19.9% exposure; 0-3: 1.19 B/1.10 R, 20.0% exposure), the largest residual motor miss by exposure×gap after fuel_type, since region E01-E06's developed-terrain relativity transfers imperfectly.

Stack both near-miss motor factors (cover_type k=200, elevation_m quintile k=200) onto the kept champion at once, since each alone raised both folds but fell short of the 0.001 keep margin (cover_type +0.00027 on 2026-10-25T03:35:36; elevation_m +0.00088 on 2026-10-25T03:40:44) and stacking has been near-additive all day.

energy_rating credibility factor on buildings and contents, since diagnostics.md flags it PERSISTENT with a large gap on buildings (level E, 10.0% exposure, A/E 1.509 B/1.839 R) and simultaneously on three contents levels (A/B/C, 14.5-17.4% exposure each) — the same field mis-ranking two lines in the same direction, and untried in the ledger.

backlog E6 (sum insured credibility factor) — untried while every other Tier 0 field has been tried or owner-ruled-out, and part2_drift.md shows a property-size shift in both directions (contents 113k emerging vs 125k developed; buildings 731k vs 680k).

credibility factor on previous_insurer (all three lines, k=200) stacked onto the kept champion — diagnostics flags it PERSISTENT on motor (5 levels) and buildings (3 levels), it's admissible and untried as a structured factor, and the drift report shows it's one of the strongest real adversarial signals on every line's core field set

Stack the two near-miss discards from this session — energy_rating (buildings+contents, 2026-10-25T03:47:04, +0.00071 both folds) and previous_insurer (2026-10-25T03:51:40, +0.00066 both folds, restricted here to motor+buildings since contents' own component D² fell in that run) — onto the kept champion, since each alone cleared both folds but missed the 0.001 margin, and today's two keeps (fuel-on-E12, cover+elevation) came from exactly this pattern.

construction_type credibility factor on buildings — diagnostics.md's PERSISTENT list against the current kept champion (e9e329e, 0.14061) flags non_standard construction (10.2% exposure, A/E 1.464 B / 1.380 R, both folds the same direction) as the largest untouched buildings miss, and it's an admissible, actuarially standard rating field no prior run has tried.

missed_payments_12m credibility factor on motor+buildings — untried in the ledger, and diagnostics.md flags it PERSISTENT with large both-fold A/E gaps on both lines (motor 6.2% exp, 1.232 B/1.178 R; buildings 6.3% exp, 1.347 B/2.065 R, the biggest gap in the buildings table).

buildings `years_at_address` credibility factor (k=200, cost basis) — diagnostics.md flags two PERSISTENT bands moving opposite ways on both folds (0-3yr under-predicted 1.248B/1.280R, 7-10yr over-predicted 0.720B/0.702R, 35% combined exposure), untried in the ledger.

retest missed_payments_12m (motor+buildings, 2026-10-25T04:01:17, discard 0.14279, +0.00075 both folds but under the 0.001 margin) on a residual basis — the factor's A/E is now measured against the champion's own stacked prediction (mirrored onto training rows as `out_tr`) instead of raw `base`, since the old raw-basis estimate likely double-counted its overlap with the already-applied `renewal_count` factor (new business lacks 12-month payment history).

pair the confirmed near-miss missed_payments_12m (motor+buildings, raw basis, discard 0.14279 at 04:01, +0.00075 both folds) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, trees_within_5m on buildings (11.7% exposure, A/E 1.316 B/1.641 R, untouched), the same two-near-miss stacking pattern that produced today's three keeps.

contents `works_from_home` credibility factor (k=200, cost basis) on top of the kept champion (27c76eb, 0.14342) — PERSISTENT at 25.0% exposure, the largest untried admissible field by exposure share, binary so low overfit risk, orthogonal to contents' existing renewal_count/energy_rating factors.
